name: architecture-skill-ab-rubric

candidate_model.comparison_unit: Each candidate is one skill or an ordered set of cooperating skills scored only on its end-to-end architecture output.
candidate_model.identity_rule: Concrete skill identities belong in the run configuration and coordinator map, never in the reusable rubric or blinded judge packet.

projection_rule: Projection fidelity compares the delivered artifact with its own declared authoritative source. A fact absent from both source and artifact is scored once as a semantic omission, not again as a projection omission.
operational_gates: Every declared authoritative source parses, type-checks, or passes the candidate's predeclared native validation using already-available tooling.

Every completed confirmatory run stays within configured token/time/tool budgets and preserves declared source/artifact files plus matching execution, callback timing, at least one native-validation log, and predeclared viewer-command/check evidence for every artifact.
Every delivered artifact opens in its documented native viewer under the configured network policy.
The artifact contains no unsafe active content or undeclared network dependency.
Applicable paths, controls, keyboard behavior, pointer behavior, desktop width, and narrow width are exercised.
Any source-rendered artifact uses the renderer and version pinned in the run configuration; an unavailable renderer is reported rather than replaced silently.
critical_errors_reported_separately: synchronous response shown after asynchronous completion
fairness_controls: Use the same model and version, system instructions, evidence snapshot, user prompt, repository access, and tool policy for both candidates.
Start every run in a fresh session and expose only the assigned candidate's configured skills.
Apply equal token, wall-time, and tool-call ceilings, then report both quality under that user-cost budget and quality among successfully completed artifacts.
Do not prescribe candidate-native formats in neutral cases; isolate explicit format requests in a separate format-fit stratum.
Grade authoritative semantics separately from projection fidelity and final-artifact usefulness.
Bind preparation inputs and blind-review bytes to externally preserved commitments; never rely only on mutable in-workspace checksum files.
Rename submissions to random IDs, remove skill names/logs/validation claims, and reconstruct independently seeded A/B order for every judge.
Preserve native formats because judges can be candidate-blind but not realistically format-blind.
Use at least three judges with mixed experience across the declared formats and record their prior format preferences.
Score only atomic gold facts required by the prompt; do not reward raw node/relationship count or a particular ontology.
Macro-average architecture families and requested-view types so one family does not dominate the result.

gold_fact_schema.adjudication: Two independent architects create and reconcile each fixture fact sheet before generation results are judged.

decision_rule.confidence_interval: 95% bootstrap interval over paired case/replicate score differences must exclude ±5 points.
decision_rule.catastrophic_error_guard: Do not declare a winner with a materially higher critical-error rate solely from its mean score.
decision_rule.otherwise: Report a capability profile by view and use case instead of one overall winner.
